description: Legitimate volume drops to 1-28k a day on Jan 3-5 (from ~450k) and recovers on Jan 6; the recovery stands out against a baseline that includes the lull.
Logins follow transactions (one per sending transaction plus failed attempts), so they show the same lull and recovery.
Disputes are filed 1 hour to 14 days after their transaction and nothing exists before Jan 1, so daily disputes ramp up (20 to 338 a day) over the first 14 days.
From Jan 18 legitimate volume falls ~20x (to 10-55k a day) while fraud stays near-constant (~262 a day), so volumes, mix and fraud share all shift; the 7-day baseline needs until Jan 25 to adjust.
Same collapse; with legitimate senders gone, the share of logins from fraudulent senders (who more often fail logins: planted signal) rises.
Same collapse; fewer receivers have activity in the prior 7 days, so the receiver ratio is null more often.
The simulation's last hours: 272 transactions, every one of them fraud.
Last day: only fraudulent senders log in, so the failed-login share jumps to 44%.
Last day: only fraud transactions, mostly to receivers with no recent activity.
